item.title: Bando calls for greater focus on weapons surrender

item.content:encoded:
​Immigration Minister and Koroba-Kopiago MP William Bando has called for continued efforts to address illegal firearms as part of broader efforts to strengthen peace and security in Papua New Guinea.

Speaking last Friday in Tari during the official launch of the provincial ‘Make Hela Safe Again - Gun Surrender Program,’ Minister Bando addressed security challenges facing Hela Province and the broader nation.

He said the presence of illegal high-powered weapons remains a concern for communities seeking lasting stability and development.

Minister Bando also highlighted the importance of weapons surrender in supporting peace and stability in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville.

He said communities and leaders across the country have a role to play in addressing the circulation of illegal firearms.

Minister Bando commended Hela Governor Philip Undialu and the Hela Provincial Government for spearheading the provincial voluntary surrender initiative.

He also announced plans to work with people in the Koroba-Lake Kopiago District to establish similar surrender programs.

The comments come as voluntary firearm surrender initiatives continue in parts of the Highlands, with dozens of illegal firearms recently handed over to authorities in Hela.

The national gun surrender amnesty has also been extended to December 25, giving people holding illegal firearms additional time to surrender them.

item.title: Simbu Hospital scales back service after Dr Waiye’s killing
item.description: Simbu health services will now operate on a half-day basis following the killing of Dr Robert Waiye. Simbu Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer Dr Ken Kassi announced the scale-down in an internal memo dated 21st September 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Simbu health services will now operate on a half-day basis following the killing of Dr Robert Waiye.

Simbu Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer Dr Ken Kassi announced the scale-down in an internal memo dated 21st September 2026.

Dr Kassi said in light of the recent killing of Dr Waiye and the petitioning of provincial authorities, SiPHA will scale down its services to half-day from Monday, 21st September 2026, until further notice.

Under the new arrangement, services will operate from 8:00AM to 12:00PM daily.

The Emergency Department will continue to operate 24 hours under its usual arrangement.

However, all consultation clinics at Sir Joseph Nombri-Kundiawa Provincial Hospital will be closed.

All special clinics, including TB, PRAPRA, physiotherapy, NOPS and others, will also be closed and only operate on arrangements with staff for the supply of drugs.

The Children's Outpatient Department [COPD] and Adult Outpatient Department [AOPD] will operate until midday only.

Public Health Directorate Headquarters and Primary Health Services will also operate up to midday.

Dr Kassi directed all officers in charge and heads of departments of the wards, operating theatre, pathology laboratory, blood bank, X-ray, CT/MRI/ultrasound, dental and pharmacy to maintain rosters and on-call arrangements to ensure patient care services continue.

The CEO stressed that the scale-down is not a holiday.

“Note that scaling down is not a holiday. SiPHA is a critical health providing government body empowered by the PHA Act 2007 and its amendments and will not tolerate health staff taking this current situation as a reason for being absent from your roster to provide Patient Care to other human beings,” Dr Kassi stated.

“The matter at hand has been placed in the hands of the law. We are grieving, terrified, and demoralized, but this must not sabotage another human life seeking our mandated life-restoring jobs and responsibilities,” he added.

Dr Kassi conveyed his deepest condolences to the family of the late Dr Robert Waiye and said SiPHA stands with the family for justice.

The general public in Simbu is advised to visit the hospital early, before 12 midday, as all services will close after midday except for the Emergency Department.

item.title: 4 missing at sea in ENBP
item.description: A search and rescue operation is continuing in East New Britain Province for four men still missing after a boat capsized near Pigeon Island on Saturday. The four, all male, were among 14 passengers travelling to the Duke of York Islands from Kokopo town on Saturday, when the vessel capsized.
item.content:encoded:
A search and rescue operation is continuing in East New Britain Province for four men still missing after a boat capsized near Pigeon Island on Saturday.

The four, all male, were among 14 passengers travelling to the Duke of York Islands from Kokopo town on Saturday, when the vessel capsized.

East New Britain Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Amanda Kates, has confirmed that nine of the passengers have been rescued while one has died.

PPC Kates said the area of search has been extended to West New Britain waters with shipping traffic travelling between East and West New Britain to help in the search of the remaining four male passengers.

Saturday’s boat mishap happened at the same location as the July 18 tragedy near Pigeon Island where 27 people including men, women and children perished.

On July 18, two boats carrying health workers, their families and friends capsized while returning from Pangpang Island in the Duke of York Islands to Kokopo.

Of the 29 people aboard both boats, 27 died, while the two skippers survived.

The East New Britain Governor - Michael Marum had since called for lessons to be learn to avoid repetition after the province lost lives in this sea incident.

Just a month before Saturday's incident, Pomio District also recorded a fatal mishap.

A 23-foot boat - Tepal, carrying 13 passengers and store goods, capsized near Saie Reef, less than a kilometre East of Pomio Station on August 21 after encountering rough seas.

Out of the 13 passengers on board, nine were rescued on the first day by local search teams, two died while two remain missing and unaccounted for.

Search teams coordinated by the Pomio District administration searched the coastline and reefs for 12 consecutive days before operations were scaled down on September 2.

The three incidents have raised concerns among authorities in the province over overloading, lack of safety gear, and travelling in rough seas.

Governor Marum had previously stated that warnings on recent disasters were issued, but many people in rural areas did not receive them, and often risk their lives at sea to access essential services like hospitals and stores.

Meanwhile, PPC Kates has urged all small craft owners and operators to ensure life jackets are carried and to check weather conditions before travelling.

item.title: Brain tumors becoming common
item.description: Brain Tumors are becoming a common cancer among children in Papua New Guinea. Paediatric Oncology at Port Moresby General Hospital, Dr Benjamin Daur revealed this when speaking about Childhood cancer on NBC Talk Back recently.
item.content:encoded:
Brain Tumors are becoming a common cancer among children in Papua New Guinea.

Paediatric Oncology at Port Moresby General Hospital, Dr Benjamin Daur revealed this when speaking about Childhood cancer on NBC Talk Back recently.

Dr Daur said childhood cancer is affecting children as young as 3 months and highlighted the cancers affecting children in the country.

“Cancer that affects children is leukemia, which is cancer of the blood. We also have a lot of cases of retinoblastoma, which is cancer of the eye.

“Lymphomas, which are cancer in the glands or the lymph nodes.” Dr Daur said.

Cancer remains a killer disease in Papua New Guinea, it continues to affect people across different age groups and placing immense pressure on the country’s health services.

Childhood cancer is all forms of cancer that is affecting our children population.

Dr Daur says Brain Tumors are now common in our children.

He said cancer can affect people at any age, the youngest patient he attended to was a 3 months’ baby and oldest an 18-year-old.

“We also have a lot of brain tumours, which is something that we haven't been seeing previously, but is becoming a bit more common nowadays.” He said.

Dr Daur stressed on the need for early detection and treatment.

item.title: Seven killed in Madang truck crash
item.description: A truck carrying several passengers has crashed at Ono village in Madang Province, killing at least seven people and seriously injuring 17 others. The crash happened at about 7 pm on Monday as the Isuzu truck, registration MAJ 316, was travelling from Bogia to Mutzing in Markham after a church gathering.
item.content:encoded:
A truck carrying several passengers has crashed at Ono village in Madang Province, killing at least seven people and seriously injuring 17 others.

The crash happened at about 7 pm on Monday as the Isuzu truck, registration MAJ 316, was travelling from Bogia to Mutzing in Markham after a church gathering.

Madang Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim, confirmed the crash and said the exact number of passengers travelling in the truck was not known.

Baim said 17 injured passengers were taken to the hospital, with seven confirmed dead, bringing the known number of people involved to 24.

Other injured passengers who were not hospitalised continued their journey to Mutzing overnight.

Police said the truck was travelling downhill and was negotiating a curve when it ran off the road, knocked down roadside barriers, and travelled about 150 metres into the bush before landing head-on

Six people died at the at the accident site, and another died later in hospital.

Baim said the truck was registered and was in good condition.

He said police would investigate the circumstances of the crash, including whether the vehicle was overloaded and whether the driver had undergone the required driver's tests before receiving a licence.

The driver was also injured and admitted to hospital.

PPC Baim said police will interview the driver after he has fully recovered and is well enough to speak, mostly likely in the next two to three days.

He has also called on new drivers to undergo proper testing through traffic officers before being issued driver's licences.

“There are no shortcuts,” Superintendent Baim said.

item.title: Displaced people of Manam Island in need of help
item.description: The Internally Displaced People of Manam Island in Madang Province are calling on the Madang Government and the National Government for immediate help as they struggle to cope with the effects of the prolonged El Nino climate. Ward councillor for Kuluguma village at Asuramba Care Centre, Charles Yanda, the told NBC News on Friday that the people are struggling every day to make ends meet.
item.content:encoded:
The Internally Displaced People of Manam Island in Madang Province are calling on the Madang Government and the National Government for immediate help as they struggle to cope with the effects of the prolonged El Nino climate.

Ward councillor for Kuluguma village at Asuramba Care Centre, Charles Yanda, the told NBC News on Friday that the people are struggling every day to make ends meet.

Their food gardens have withered, and all their water sources have dried up.

They are now resorting to the sea for their supply of water.

"All three care centres, Asuramaba, Pottsdam, and Mangem, are facing the same problem.

"Whatever food crops we have in our gardens have died. Our old water pumps need replacements as they are no longer working.

"The longer this El Nino period continues, we will be faced with severe hunger. Even our children are no longer attending classes full time because there is no fresh water in the schools and food is becoming scarce. We need food rations and clean drinking water for now," Yanda said.

He said the current situation could trigger off an outbreak of diseases at the care centres.

Councillor Yanda stated," We are worried that if there is an outbreak of some kind of diseases here, we have no medicines at our aid posts. Our aid posts are empty. We are often just given prescriptions and told to buy medicines at the market at Malala or from the pharmacies in town, which are quite expensive.

Mr Yanda said ward councillors and recorders in the care centres, and on the islands, Manam and Boisa have compiled reports on the situations in their respective communities, which they have furnished to the President of Iabu Local Level Government, Kenny Boli; to present to the Madang Provincial Government for possible assistance.

The current household population captured the El Nino report is 18, 337, inclduding Manam and Boisa islands.

Last week, Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa announced that the Madang Provincial Government was scaling down on sectoral funding support in the Provincial Administration.

He said the Madang government was shifting its focus more towards the province's El Nino response efforts with support from the National Government.

item.title: MS-22 police barracks in Koroba nears completion
item.description: Construction on the Mobile Squad 22 (MS 22) Police Barracks in Koroba is progressing, with commissioning scheduled for December. The project is being funded by the Koroba-Lake Kopiago District Development Authority (DDA) as part of its ongoing push to reinforce law and order in the district. In response to the request, two vehicles have been officially handed over to the Koroba-Kopiago police to b
item.content:encoded:
Construction on the Mobile Squad 22 (MS 22) Police Barracks in Koroba is progressing, with commissioning scheduled for December. The project is being funded by the Koroba-Lake Kopiago District Development Authority (DDA) as part of its ongoing push to reinforce law and order in the district.

In response to the request, two vehicles have been officially handed over to the Koroba-Kopiago police to boost law and order operations in the district.

Koroba-Kopiago MP William Bando thanked Minister for Police Sir John Pundari and the Hela Provincial Government for their prompt response to his request.

"The MS 22 Police Barracks construction currently underway is solely funded by our DDA—we have received no aid from the Police Department. While other districts in the province have yet to build similar facilities, these two vehicles will directly complement our groundwork."

MP Bando revealed that the DDA spends approximately K400,000 every month consistently for the past four years solely on maintaining law and justice operations across the district. ​ MP Bando acknowledged Hela Governor Philip Undialu for allocating 10 police houses to the district under the Hela Police Housing Rollout Program.

​"Law and order are our top priority because people can only respect and enjoy essential services when there is peace.

"Koroba-Lake Kopiago was once heavily impacted by lawlessness, but peace is returning because of the priority we have given to the law and justice sector." MP Bando said.

item.title: NCD citizen surrenders firearm
item.description: A good citizen in the National Capital District has been commended by Commander for the National Capital District and Central Province, Benjamin Turi, for willingly surrendering an unlicensed firearm. Turi thanked Seven Mile Police Station Commander Inspector Henry Map and his officers after receiving the surrendered weapon—a .38 calibre revolver.
item.content:encoded:
A good citizen in the National Capital District has been commended by Commander for the National Capital District and Central Province, Benjamin Turi, for willingly surrendering an unlicensed firearm.

Turi thanked Seven Mile Police Station Commander Inspector Henry Map and his officers after receiving the surrendered weapon—a .38 calibre revolver.

While acknowledging the work of the police station commanders and officers across the command, Turi challenged them to increase public awareness regarding the ongoing gun amnesty program in their respective operational areas.

“Before we look elsewhere, I want to call on my police officers to inspect themselves and their circles, and to bring forward any illegal firearms they or their acquaintances may possess.

“The gun amnesty period has been extended to December 25, 2026, as per a media statement from Police Minister Sir John Pundari—a directive we are all expected to support to ensure illegal weapons are turned in. These offensive weapons will only lead to trouble,” Turi said.

He said that to date, two individuals in the NCD have voluntarily surrendered their firearms and others are likely to follow.

The gun amnesty program was launched on February 27, 2026, by Police Minister Sir John Pundari who has travelled throughout the country witnessing the surrender of illegal weapons, expressed satisfaction with the results and reiterated his public call for anyone still holding illegal firearms to turn them in.
